key_insight: Partial quantum error correction can be used as a programmable primitive to turn logical noise into a controlled dissipative channel for open-system simulation.
engineering_relevance: This reduces the need for explicit bath ancillas and suggests a more resource-efficient route to compiling target dissipators into fault-tolerant quantum hardware.
method: Run one fault-tolerant error-correction cycle to induce a logical CPTP map.
Randomize decoder/recovery choices to generate a tunable family of logical channels.
Mix these channels to realize desired Kraus-channel combinations and effective dissipation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an accuracy criterion for multi-step simulation that sets code distance so uncontrolled logical errors stay below a chosen fraction of the intended dissipation per step.
watch_item: Practical use depends on carefully balancing code distance and residual logical error so unwanted noise does not overwhelm the programmed dissipative dynamics.
paper_title: Programmable Dissipation via Partial Quantum Error Correction
